newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds recoup losses on technical bounce.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds recoup losses on technical bounce.

text.p: Argentine bonds recovered most of their early losses late Wednesday as short-covering emerged at key technical levels.

Bonds were sharply lower at the opening as the sour mood of recent sessions maintained the market in its grip. But traders said that when Argentina's FRB dropped as low as 79-1/2 buyer interest emerged.
The FRB due 2005 finished just 1/4 down at 80-3/8.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was at 117.49, down $0.06, after having traded as much as $0.80 lower earlier in the day.
Despite the bounce, uncertainties around corruption accusations by former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo and the softer Mexican peso lingered Wednesday.
"In these days in the market there is a lot of noise, a lot of talk and little activity. Investors are waiting hesitantly for the moment to return to the market," said an analyst.

The trader added that even though the market came off lows, the session's activity was still dominated by trading between brokerages as opposed to actual buying. Still, judging from the afternoon recovery the trader predicted prices could open firmer on Thursday.
Traders said there was also some support this session from firmer U.S. treasuries.
In the money markets, call money fell to 7.25 percent from 7.35 percent.
-- Axel Bugge, Buenos Aires Newsroom, 541 3180668 (c) Reuters Limited 1996
